metaDescription: Four Hermitlux countertop dishwashers compared: the 5-setting color-screen unit, the 7-program Self-Clean model, the glass-door unit and the basic washer.
expertTake: The five-setting color-screen model is the best overall because it states the largest capacity and the clearest efficiency figures. The basic five-program unit is the value pick. Large families and anyone washing big cookware should skip every model in this small-cube range.
introParagraphs: A maker with only four listings is easy to read once you know what separates them. The bodies are almost the same size, the tanks are the same 5 liters in most cases, and the differences sit in the controls, the program list and how clearly the capacity is stated.

These are small tank-fed washers for light daily loads. They suit couples, dorms and compact kitchens, and they suit nobody who cooks for a crowd. Here is how the four compare and where each one earns its place.

products.name: Hermitlux Countertop Dishwasher, 5 Place Settings, Color Screen

specList.label: Energy
specList.value: 61.30 kWh per year, 43 percent below standard models

products.description:
This is the largest and most informative Hermitlux. It states a capacity of five full place settings in a body of 17.3 by 17.1 by 18.1 inches, which is a clearer claim than the item counts that most small washers use. Color touch keys and a color screen replace the button row, so choosing a program is a one-touch task.

The efficiency numbers are specific: the listing quotes 61.30 kWh per year, 43 percent lower than standard models, and 1.139 gallons of water per cycle. Eight washing programs and a 5 liter built-in tank round it out. Against the seven-program Hermitlux below it adds a display and a larger stated capacity, while the cube is a few tenths of an inch bigger on each side.

In daily ownership the color screen is the feature owners tend to notice first, because it removes the guesswork about which cycle is running. The tank still needs filling by hand, the filter still needs rinsing and the door still needs to be left cracked after a wash. For a household that wants clear controls and clear numbers, it is the easiest of the four to recommend. Its extra width of about half an inch over the 16.85 inch cubes is the only real penalty, and it only matters on a very tight counter.
products.bestFor: Couples and small households that want clear capacity figures and an easy screen.

products.name: Hermitlux Countertop Dishwasher, 7 Programs with Self-Clean

specList.label: Programs
specList.value: Standard, Quick, Strong, ECO, Fruit, Self-Clean, Glass

specList.label: Water use
specList.value: 5L per cycle, up to 83 percent less than handwashing

products.description:
The seven-program model is the one with the cleaning cycles. The list is Standard, Quick, Strong, ECO, Fruit, Self-Clean and Glass, which gives owners a dedicated glass program and a chamber clean in addition to the basics. A Strong cycle handles heavier soil, and Self-Clean helps keep a small tank machine from gathering grease.

The maker also quotes 5 liters per cycle and a saving of up to 83 percent in water compared with handwashing. The body measures 16.85 by 16.73 by 18.23 inches, taller than the other cubes by a fifth of an inch, which matters under low cabinets. Compared with the five-setting color-screen model it gives up the display and the stated place-setting count, but keeps most of the programs.

Practical care is the usual routine. Run Self-Clean monthly with dishwasher cleaner, rinse the filter every few loads and dry the chamber. Because the machine runs on standard 120V power, it plugs into a normal outlet. That makes it a workable choice for a camper kitchen where water is the scarce resource, provided the inverter can carry the heating load. Check the wattage in the manual before running it off batteries.
products.bestFor: Cooks who want Strong and Self-Clean cycles in a compact body.
pros: Seven programs including Strong, Self-Clean and Glass
5 liters per cycle with a stated water saving
cons: No stated place-setting count in the listing

products.name: Hermitlux Countertop Dishwasher, Glass Door, 4 Place Settings
products.description:
This model combines a stated capacity of four place settings with a transparent glass door. Watching the spray arm lets you see whether plates are blocking the spray, which is a quick way for a new owner to learn how to load a small chamber. Five programs include Standard Cleaning, Fast Cleaning and ECO.

The cube is 16.85 by 16.73 by 18.03 inches and runs on 120V. Against the 7-program Hermitlux it has fewer cycles and no Self-Clean, and against the color-screen model it holds one fewer place setting. What you gain is the glass door and the lower position on the price ladder.

Glass shows spots, so wipe it weekly, and keep an eye on the seal for grit. Treat the tank like a food container, emptying and drying it after use. It suits first-time buyers who want to see the wash and learn the machine. After a few weeks of watching the spray, most owners stop looking and stack the rack by habit, which is exactly the point of a learning aid. A second benefit is that you can spot a stuck spray arm without opening the door mid-cycle.

products.name: Hermitlux Portable Countertop Dishwasher, 5 Programs, 14 Water Jets

specList.label: Spray
specList.value: 14 water jets, top and bottom, 360 degree

products.description:
The simplest Hermitlux lists five programs, Standard, Quick, Strong, ECO and Fruit, and relies on its spray design to do the work. Spray arms with 14 water jets fire from both the top and the bottom, aiming for 360 degree coverage inside the chamber. The Strong program is the one that sets it above a single-speed machine.

The body is the familiar 16.85 by 16.73 by 18.03 inch cube with a 5 liter tank on 120V power. Against the glass-door model it drops the transparent door and the stated four-setting capacity, and against the 7-program model it has no Glass or Self-Clean program. In return you get the lowest cost in the lineup and the least to learn.

Ownership is the plain routine: fill, run, drain and dry. Run Strong for dried-on food and Quick for cups. Rinse the filter regularly, because the 14 jets are small and can clog with debris. If a plate comes out with a clean band and a dirty band, suspect a blocked jet or a filter that needs rinsing before blaming the program. That pattern points to a maintenance fix, not a faulty machine.
products.bestFor: Single users who want the lowest cost and a simple Strong cycle.
pros: Lowest cost among the four Hermitlux models
14 water jets spray from top and bottom
cons: Small jets can clog if the filter is neglected

buyingCriteria.explanation: Place settings are the honest way to size a dishwasher. The color-screen Hermitlux claims five settings and the glass-door model claims four, while the other two give no count. A five-setting claim in a 17.3 inch wide body is more useful than a bare item count. Treat any model with no capacity figure as a one or two person machine. Put your own plates beside the stated interior dimensions, because dinner plates above about 10 inches fit poorly in every small cube. Bowls and mugs stack more easily than plates, so a household that eats mostly from bowls gets more from the same chamber.

The seven-program model adds Self-Clean and Glass, and the five-program models cover Standard, Quick, Strong, ECO and Fruit. Self-Clean is the extra that pays off in small tank machines, because grease builds in a small chamber. If you only wash plates and cups, five is enough. If you cook greasy food, the extra Strong and Self-Clean cycles earn their place. A common mistake is to run Quick on every load to save time, then find a film of grease on the plates. Quick is for cups and glasses, Standard is for ordinary plates, and Strong is for pans and dried sauces. Learn those three and the other modes become optional.

The color-screen model quotes 61.30 kWh per year and 1.139 gallons of water per cycle, while the seven-program model quotes 5 liters per cycle. These figures give a way to compare machines, though they come from the seller and depend on how the test was run. They matter most for people on a water meter or an RV tank. A cycle that uses 5 liters is cheap in water but still sends that volume to a drain, so a camper's gray tank fills after a few loads. Do the arithmetic against your own tank size and washing habits before trusting any saving claim.

A color screen with touch keys makes program choice obvious, which helps guests and occasional users. Button rows are cheaper and often fine. The glass-door model adds a visual check of the wash. Pick controls you will not misread at the end of a long day. Touch panels can be sensitive to wet fingers, so dry your hands before pressing them, and wipe the panel with a barely damp cloth. Mechanical buttons are easier to feel but show less information, so the right choice depends on how you use the machine.

The cubes run from 16.85 by 16.73 inches to 17.3 by 17.1 inches, with heights of 18.03, 18.1 and 18.23 inches. Those fractions matter under low wall cabinets. Measure the clearance, and remember the door needs space to swing. Allow a hand's width behind the body for the hose and the steam vent, and keep the machine a few inches from a stove or toaster. Heat and steam from neighbors shorten the life of the seal and the electronics.

More water jets spread coverage, and the basic model lists 14 jets firing from both the top and the bottom. A good spray design still needs good loading, because stacked plates block jets. Lean items the same way and keep bowls face-down. Small jets are also easier to clog than large nozzles, so a clean filter matters more here than in a big machine. Look into the spray arm every month for rice or seeds, and clear any blocked jet with a toothpick, never a metal pin.

howWeEvaluated.title: Capacity claims
howWeEvaluated.description: We compared stated place settings across the four models, with the color-screen unit at five and the glass-door unit at four. Models with no count lost points. Honest capacity matters more than item totals.

howWeEvaluated.title: Efficiency data
howWeEvaluated.description: We read the quoted energy and water figures, noting that the color-screen model gives both while the others give less. The seller supplies these numbers, so we treated them as claims, not measurements. A model that publishes numbers gives buyers a way to compare, and a model that publishes none leaves them guessing, so publication itself earned a small amount of credit.

howWeEvaluated.title: Program breadth
howWeEvaluated.description: We counted the useful programs, with Self-Clean, Glass and Strong as real differences. Duplicated quick modes counted once. The 7-program model scored highest. We also asked whether a program does something the user can feel, such as removing grease or protecting glass, and discounted modes that only change the time on the display.

howWeEvaluated.title: Controls
howWeEvaluated.description: We looked at the screen, the glass door and the button layout. The color screen earned credit for clarity, and the glass door earned credit for helping new users.

howWeEvaluated.title: Footprint
howWeEvaluated.description: We compared dimensions, from the 16.85 inch cubes to the 17.3 inch wide color-screen model. Based on the spec sheet and owner feedback patterns, extra size was worth it only when capacity grew with it.

cards.text: The five-setting Hermitlux uses color touch keys and gives clear efficiency figures. It suits people who like digital feedback and want the largest stated capacity.

cards.text: The four-setting Hermitlux lets you see the spray arm and the load. It suits new owners who want to learn how to stack the rack.

howToChoose.note: Choose the screen for clarity and the glass door for learning. Both are tank-fed cubes of nearly the same size, so neither is a mistake, and the decision comes down to whether you want numbers on a display or a view of the spray.

maintenance.why: Debris clogs the screen and small spray jets. A clean filter keeps coverage even. Twist it out, rinse under running water and brush off film with a soft brush before you seat it again.
Standing water breeds odor. Leave the lid open to dry.

maintenance.task: Wipe the glass door and seal
maintenance.why: Spots and residue collect. A clean seal also keeps the door closing properly.

maintenance.task: Run Self-Clean or a hot cycle
maintenance.why: Grease builds in a small chamber. Use dishwasher cleaner and never hand soap.
A kinked or climbing hose leaves water behind and causes odor.

faq.q: How many place settings does a Hermitlux hold?
faq.a: The color-screen model states five and the glass-door model states four. The other two listings give no count, so treat them as one or two person machines.
The seven-program model lists Self-Clean, along with Strong and Glass. The five-program models do not.

faq.q: Do they need a faucet connection?
faq.a: No. All four use a 5 liter built-in tank. You fill it by hand and run a drain hose to a sink or container. That is convenient for rentals, though it means a jug and a steady pour for every load. Keep a spouted measuring jug beside the machine so filling never turns into a spill.

They are the seller's own figures under standard test conditions. Use them to compare machines, and expect real results to vary with how you load. Half-empty runs waste water and power, so wait for a reasonable stack, and avoid running the same dishes twice because they came out dirty after an overloaded cycle.

faq.q: Can I run it on an RV inverter?
faq.a: The listings state 120V. Check the wattage in the manual against your inverter's continuous rating, because heating water is the biggest load.

faq.q: What should I avoid putting in?
faq.a: Large pots, baking sheets and thin plastics on hot programs. Use dishwasher detergent only, and never hand soap, because suds overflow the door and can foul the pump. Cast iron and nonstick pans are better washed by hand in any case, since detergent strips seasoning and coatings.
